subject: General Information
question: What type of state does the 1987 Philippine Constitution declare the Philippines to be?

choices.text: Democratic and republican state
Federal and parliamentary state
Unitary and monarchical state
Socialist and democratic state

explanation: Article II, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution explicitly states: 'The Philippines is a democratic and republican State. Sovereignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them.' This foundational principle establishes the nature of the Philippine state.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, what is the term of office of the President of the Philippines?

choices.text: Six years, not eligible for re-election
Five years, not eligible for re-election
Four years, eligible for one re-election
Six years, eligible for one re-election

explanation: Article VII, Section 4 provides that 'The President and the Vice-President shall be elected by direct vote of the people for a term of six years.' The same section further states that 'The President shall not be eligible for any reelection,' making the six-year single term the constitutional rule.

subject: General Information
question: What is the term of office of a Senator under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, and how many consecutive terms may a Senator serve?

choices.text: Six years; not more than two consecutive terms
Three years; not more than three consecutive terms
Four years; not more than two consecutive terms
Six years; not more than three consecutive terms

explanation: Article VI, Section 4 states that 'The term of office of the Senators shall be six years.' The same section provides that 'No Senator shall serve for more than two consecutive terms.' Voluntary renunciation does not interrupt continuity of service.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, what is the minimum age requirement to vote in Philippine elections?

choices.text: 18 years old
21 years old
15 years old
16 years old

explanation: Article V, Section 1 provides that suffrage may be exercised by all citizens 'who are at least eighteen years of age.' The same provision adds that no literacy, property, or other substantive requirement shall be imposed on the exercise of suffrage.

subject: General Information
question: Which body has the exclusive power to initiate all cases of impeachment under the 1987 Philippine Constitution?

choices.text: The Senate
The Supreme Court
The Ombudsman
The House of Representatives

explanation: Article XI, Section 3(1) expressly states that 'The House of Representatives shall have the exclusive power to initiate all cases of impeachment.' The Senate, by contrast, has the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, a member of the House of Representatives is elected for a term of three years and may not serve for more than how many consecutive terms?

choices.text: Three consecutive terms
Four consecutive terms
Two consecutive terms
No term limit is specified

explanation: Article VI, Section 7 provides that members of the House of Representatives 'shall be elected for a term of three years' and that 'No Member of the House of Representatives shall serve for more than three consecutive terms.' Voluntary renunciation does not count as an interruption.

subject: General Information
question: What vote is required in the Senate to convict an impeached official under the 1987 Philippine Constitution?

choices.text: A simple majority of all members of the Senate
Three-fourths of all members of the Senate
Two-thirds of members present and voting
Two-thirds of all members of the Senate

explanation: Article XI, Section 3(6) states that 'No person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate.' When the President is on trial, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court presides but does not vote.

subject: General Information
question: Which of the following officials is NOT among those who may be removed by impeachment under the 1987 Philippine Constitution?

choices.text: The Ombudsman
Members of the Constitutional Commissions
The Secretary of Justice
Members of the Supreme Court

explanation: Article XI, Section 2 lists the impeachable officers as the President, Vice-President, Members of the Supreme Court, Members of the Constitutional Commissions, and the Ombudsman. The Secretary of Justice is not on this list; cabinet secretaries may be removed by other means provided by law, but not by impeachment.

subject: General Information
question: The 1987 Constitution provides that Members of the Supreme Court and judges of lower courts shall hold office during good behavior until they reach what age?

choices.text: 65 years old
70 years old
75 years old
60 years old

explanation: Article VIII, Section 11 states that 'The Members of the Supreme Court and judges of lower courts shall hold office during good behavior until they reached the age of seventy years or become incapacitated to discharge the duties of their office.' This mandatory retirement age ensures a balance between judicial experience and periodic renewal.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, what is the minimum age to be appointed as a Member of the Supreme Court?

choices.text: At least 35 years of age
At least 45 years of age
At least 50 years of age
At least 40 years of age

explanation: Article VIII, Section 7(1) requires that a Member of the Supreme Court 'must be at least forty years of age, and must have been for fifteen years or more, a judge of a lower court or engaged in the practice of law in the Philippines.' The member must also be a natural-born citizen.

subject: General Information
question: According to the 1987 Philippine Constitution, what does Article II, Section 3 state about civilian authority over the military?

choices.text: Civilian authority is, at all times, supreme over the military
The military may exercise civilian authority during times of national emergency
The President shares command authority with the Chief of Staff
Military authority takes precedence in times of war

explanation: Article II, Section 3 explicitly declares that 'Civilian authority is, at all times, supreme over the military.' It further states that the Armed Forces of the Philippines is the protector of the people and the State, and its goal is to secure the sovereignty of the State and the integrity of the national territory.

subject: General Information
question: The 1987 Philippine Constitution provides that the Supreme Court shall be composed of a Chief Justice and how many Associate Justices?

choices.text: Twelve Associate Justices
Fifteen Associate Justices
Ten Associate Justices
Fourteen Associate Justices

explanation: Article VIII, Section 4(1) states that 'The Supreme Court shall be composed of a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices.' The Court may sit en banc or, in its discretion, in divisions of three, five, or seven Members.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, what is the minimum age requirement to run for President of the Philippines?

choices.text: At least 35 years of age on the day of the election
At least 45 years of age on the day of the election
At least 40 years of age on the day of the election
At least 30 years of age on the day of the election

explanation: Article VII, Section 2 provides that 'No person may be elected President unless he is a natural-born citizen of the Philippines, a registered voter, able to read and write, at least forty years of age on the day of the election, and a resident of the Philippines for at least ten years immediately preceding such election.'

subject: General Information
question: Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution guarantees the right of the people to what kind of ecology?

choices.text: A balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature
Pristine and undisturbed ecology free from human intervention
A productive and industrialized ecology for national development
A protected ecology managed solely by the State

explanation: Article II, Section 16 declares that 'The State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.' This provision is the constitutional basis for environmental protection in the Philippines.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, the Bill of Rights (Article III, Section 1) provides that no person shall be deprived of life, liberty, or property without which of the following?

choices.text: Approval by the Supreme Court
An act of Congress
Due process of law
An executive order

explanation: Article III, Section 1 states: 'No person shall be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law, nor shall any person be denied the equal protection of the laws.' This dual guarantee — due process and equal protection — forms the cornerstone of the Bill of Rights.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, which among the following is a ground for impeachment of the President, Vice-President, and Members of the Supreme Court?

choices.text: Betrayal of public trust
Inefficiency and incompetence in the performance of official duties
Gross discourtesy to subordinates
Failure to file the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth

explanation: Article XI, Section 2 enumerates the grounds for impeachment as: culpable violation of the Constitution, treason, bribery, graft and corruption, other high crimes, or betrayal of public trust. Inefficiency, gross discourtesy, and failure to file SALN are administrative offenses addressed through other proceedings.

subject: General Information
question: The 1987 Philippine Constitution declares in Article II, Section 7 that in its relations with other states, the paramount consideration of Philippine foreign policy shall be which of the following?

choices.text: Economic growth and foreign investment attraction
Military alliances and collective defense
Adherence to international organizations and treaties
National sovereignty, territorial integrity, national interest, and the right to self-determination

explanation: Article II, Section 7 states that 'The State shall pursue an independent foreign policy. In its relations with other states, the paramount consideration shall be national sovereignty, territorial integrity, national interest, and the right to self-determination.' This provision underlies the Philippines' independent foreign policy.

subject: General Information
question: Under Article IX-B of the 1987 Constitution, appointments in the civil service shall be made according to merit and fitness determined, as far as practicable, by what means — except for positions which are policy-determining, primarily confidential, or highly technical?

choices.text: Presidential appointment without other requirements
Educational attainment alone
Competitive examination
Seniority and length of service

explanation: Article IX-B, Section 1(2) provides that 'Appointments in the civil service shall be made only according to merit and fitness to be determined, as far as practicable, and, except as to positions which are policy-determining, primarily confidential, or highly technical, by competitive examination.' This merit system is the backbone of the Philippine civil service.

subject: General Information
question: The 1987 Constitution, Article III, Section 4 prohibits the passage of any law abridging which of the following rights?

choices.text: The right to bear arms
The right to education and literacy
The freedom of speech, of expression, or of the press, or the right of the people peaceably to assemble and petition the Government
The right to economic livelihood and employment

explanation: Article III, Section 4 states: 'No law shall be passed abridging the freedom of speech, of expression, or of the press, or the right of the people peaceably to assemble and petition the Government for redress of grievances.' This provision protects fundamental political and civil liberties.

subject: General Information
question: Under Article IX-B of the 1987 Constitution, a member of the Civil Service Commission must be a natural-born citizen and, at the time of appointment, at least how old, with what qualification?

choices.text: At least 40 years of age with at least 10 years of legal practice
At least 45 years of age with 15 years of civil service experience
At least 35 years of age with proven capacity for public administration
At least 30 years of age with a master's degree in public administration

explanation: Article IX-B, Section 1(1) provides that the Civil Service Commission shall be composed of a Chairman and two Commissioners who 'must be natural-born citizens of the Philippines and, at the time of their appointment, at least thirty-five years of age, with proven capacity for public administration, and must not have been candidates for any elective position in the elections immediately preceding their appointment.'

subject: General Information
question: Article VII, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution provides that a person who has succeeded to the presidency and served as such for more than four years shall be qualified to run for President at any time?

choices.text: Yes, after sitting out one term
Yes, if endorsed by a political party
No, such a person is never qualified for election to the presidency
Yes, since the constitutional prohibition applies only to duly-elected Presidents

explanation: Article VII, Section 4 states: 'No person who has succeeded as President and has served as such for more than four years shall be qualified for election to the same office at any time.' This provision ensures that one who effectively served a near-full presidential term cannot seek another mandate.

subject: General Information
question: Under Article III, Section 7 of the 1987 Constitution, the right of the people to information on matters of public concern shall be recognized. This right covers access to what?

choices.text: Official records and documents pertaining to official acts, transactions, or decisions, as well as government research data used as basis for policy development
Only published government reports and audited financial statements
All government communications including those classified as state secrets
Only court decisions and legislative records

explanation: Article III, Section 7 states that the right to information covers access 'to official records, and to documents, and papers pertaining to official acts, transactions, or decisions, as well as to government research data used as basis for policy development,' subject to such limitations as may be provided by law.

subject: General Information
question: What is the declared policy of the State under Section 2 of Republic Act No. 6713?

choices.text: To promote efficiency and reduce costs in government operations
To promote a high standard of ethics in public service and require public officials to uphold public interest over personal interest
To impose strict criminal penalties for all forms of corruption
To professionalize the civil service through mandatory examinations

explanation: Section 2 of RA 6713 declares that 'It is the policy of the State to promote a high standard of ethics in public service. Public officials and employees shall at all times be accountable to the people and shall discharge their duties with utmost responsibility, integrity, competence, and loyalty, act with patriotism and justice, lead modest lives, and uphold public interest over personal interest.'

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 6713, which norm of conduct requires public officials and employees to 'lead modest lives appropriate to their positions and income' and prohibits extravagant display of wealth?

choices.text: Simple living
Justness and sincerity
Commitment to public interest
Professionalism

explanation: Section 4(A)(h) of RA 6713 establishes the norm of 'Simple living,' under which 'Public officials and employees and their families shall lead modest lives appropriate to their positions and income. They shall not indulge in extravagant or ostentatious display of wealth in any form.'

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 6713, which agency has the primary responsibility for the administration and enforcement of the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees?

choices.text: The Office of the Ombudsman
The Department of Justice
The Civil Service Commission
The Office of the President

explanation: Section 12 of RA 6713 states that 'The Civil Service Commission shall have the primary responsibility for the administration and enforcement of this Act.' The CSC transmits cases for prosecution to proper authorities while retaining authority to institute administrative actions and disciplinary measures.

subject: General Information
question: Under Section 8 of RA 6713, all public officials and employees are required to file a Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN). Which of the following categories is expressly EXCLUDED from this requirement?

choices.text: Permanent employees in the national government
Those who serve in an honorary capacity, laborers, and casual or temporary workers
Local government officials
Military and police personnel

explanation: Section 8(A) of RA 6713 provides that 'All public officials and employees, except those who serve in an honorary capacity, laborers and casual or temporary workers, shall file under oath their Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth and a Disclosure of Business Interests and Financial Connections.' The exclusion applies to honorary capacity servers, laborers, and casual or temporary workers.

subject: General Information
question: Under Section 9 of RA 6713, when a conflict of interest arises, a public official must resign from any private business enterprise within how many days from assumption of office?

choices.text: Fifteen (15) days
Sixty (60) days
Ninety (90) days
Thirty (30) days

explanation: Section 9 of RA 6713 provides that when a conflict of interest arises, the public official 'shall resign from his position in any private business enterprise within thirty (30) days from his assumption of office and/or divest himself of his shareholdings or interest within sixty (60) days from such assumption.'

subject: General Information
question: RA 6713 defines 'relatives' for the purpose of prohibitions on undue favors as persons related to a public official within what degree of consanguinity or affinity?

choices.text: Within the fourth civil degree
Within the third civil degree
Within the second civil degree
Within the fifth civil degree

explanation: Section 3(k) of RA 6713 defines 'Relatives' as 'any and all persons related to a public official or employee within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity, including bilas, inso and balae.' This definition is used in applying prohibitions on nepotism and undue favors.

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 6713, what is the norm of conduct that requires public officials to 'extend prompt, courteous, and adequate service to the public' and to avoid red tape?

choices.text: Commitment to public interest
Nationalism and patriotism
Justness and sincerity
Responsiveness to the public

explanation: Section 4(A)(e) of RA 6713 establishes 'Responsiveness to the public' as a norm of conduct, requiring officials to 'extend prompt, courteous, and adequate service to the public' and to 'avoid red tape and develop an understanding and appreciation of the socio-economic conditions prevailing in the country.' Officials must also ensure openness of information and encourage suggestions.

subject: General Information
question: Section 7(d) of RA 6713 prohibits public officials from soliciting or accepting gifts. Under the law's definition, which of the following is EXCLUDED from the definition of 'gift'?

choices.text: A gift of significant monetary value given during Christmas by a contractor
A loan extended to a public official by a company whose application is under review
Any entertainment given by a person whose transaction is being processed by the official
An unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value not given in anticipation of, or in exchange for, a favor

explanation: Section 3(c) of RA 6713 defines 'Gift' broadly but expressly excludes 'an unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value not given in anticipation of, or in exchange for, a favor from a public official or employee.' Section 3(d) further clarifies that receiving any gift 'even on the occasion of a family celebration or national festivity like Christmas' is covered if the value is not nominal or if it is given in anticipation of a favor.

subject: General Information
question: Under Section 11 of RA 6713, what is the maximum fine that may be imposed for a violation of the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards?

choices.text: The equivalent of three months' salary
The equivalent of six months' salary
The equivalent of twelve months' salary
A fixed fine of fifty thousand pesos

explanation: Section 11(a) of RA 6713 provides that a public official or employee committing any violation of the Act 'shall be punished with a fine not exceeding the equivalent of six (6) months' salary.' The penalty may also include imprisonment, depending on the nature and gravity of the violation.

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 6713, the norm of 'Nationalism and patriotism' requires public officials and employees to do which of the following?

choices.text: Prioritize foreign investment and global partnerships above local interests
Use English as the primary language in all official communications
Join civic organizations and attend national celebrations
Be loyal to the Republic and to the Filipino people, promote the use of locally produced goods, and defend Philippine sovereignty against foreign intrusion

explanation: Section 4(A)(f) of RA 6713 defines 'Nationalism and patriotism' as the obligation to 'at all times be loyal to the Republic and to the Filipino people, promote the use of locally produced goods, resources and technology and encourage appreciation and pride of country and people. They shall endeavor to maintain and defend Philippine sovereignty against foreign intrusion.'

subject: General Information
question: RA 6713 defines 'divestment' as which of the following?

choices.text: The temporary suspension of business interests while in public office

The transfer of title or disposal of interest in property by voluntarily, completely and actually depriving or dispossessing oneself of his right or title to it in favor of a person other than his spouse and relatives
The declaration of all business interests in the SALN without transfer of ownership
The placement of private property in a blind trust managed by a government trustee

explanation: Section 3(j) of RA 6713 defines 'Divestment' as 'the transfer of title or disposal of interest in property by voluntarily, completely and actually depriving or dispossessing oneself of his right or title to it in favor of a person or persons other than his spouse and relatives as defined in this Act.' Mere declaration or blind trust does not satisfy this requirement.

subject: General Information
question: Under Section 4(A)(g) of RA 6713, the norm of 'Commitment to democracy' requires public officials and employees to manifest by deeds which of the following?

choices.text: Supremacy of the military in national security matters
Supremacy of civilian authority over the military, and to put loyalty to country above loyalty to persons or party
Loyalty to their political party and its agenda above all else
Compliance with orders of the President regardless of constitutionality

explanation: Section 4(A)(g) of RA 6713 requires public officials to 'commit themselves to the democratic way of life and values, maintain the principle of public accountability, and manifest by deeds the supremacy of civilian authority over the military. They shall at all times uphold the Constitution and put loyalty to country above loyalty to persons or party.'

subject: General Information
question: The SALN under RA 6713 requires disclosure of assets, liabilities, net worth, and financial and business interests of the public official and whose other dependents?

choices.text: All relatives within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity
All household members regardless of age or relationship
Parents and siblings of the public official
Spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age living in their households

explanation: Section 8 of RA 6713 specifies that the SALN must cover the public official's 'assets, liabilities, net worth and financial and business interests including those of their spouses and of unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age living in their households.' Section 3(g) reinforces this by defining 'Family of public officials or employees' as 'their spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age.'

subject: General Information
question: The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) of the Philippines was created under which article of the 1987 Constitution?

choices.text: Article XIII (Social Justice and Human Rights)
Article XI (Accountability of Public Officers)
Article IX-B (Civil Service Commission)
Article III (Bill of Rights)

explanation: The Commission on Human Rights was created under Article XIII (Social Justice and Human Rights), Section 17-18 of the 1987 Constitution. Section 17(1) states 'There is hereby created an independent office called the Commission on Human Rights.' The CHR was formally constituted on May 5, 1987 by virtue of Executive Order No. 163.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, the Commission on Human Rights has the mandate to investigate all forms of human rights violations involving what category of rights?

choices.text: Economic, social, and cultural rights only
Civil and political rights
All rights including environmental and labor rights
Rights of overseas Filipino workers only

explanation: Article XIII, Section 18(1) of the 1987 Constitution grants the CHR power to 'Investigate, on its own or on complaint by any party, all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights.' The CHR's constitutional mandate is thus focused on civil and political rights, though it may address other rights through legal measures.

subject: General Information
question: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in which year?
explanation: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on December 10, 1948 through Resolution 217A. December 10 is commemorated annually as International Human Rights Day. The UDHR is the foundational international instrument proclaiming universal human rights.
reference: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), UN General Assembly Resolution 217A

subject: General Information
question: One of the powers of the Commission on Human Rights under the 1987 Constitution is to exercise visitorial powers over which of the following?

choices.text: Private corporations and business establishments
Jails, prisons, or detention facilities
Government-owned and controlled corporations
Schools and educational institutions

explanation: Article XIII, Section 18(4) of the 1987 Constitution grants the CHR the power to 'Exercise visitorial powers over jails, prisons, or detention facilities.' This power allows the CHR to inspect conditions of confinement to help prevent and detect human rights violations against persons deprived of liberty.

subject: General Information
question: The concept of 'human dignity' as recognized by the UDHR holds that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. In the 1987 Philippine Constitution, which article and section expressly states that 'The State values the dignity of every human person and guarantees full respect for human rights'?

choices.text: Article III, Section 1
Article II, Section 11
Article XIII, Section 1
Article XI, Section 1

explanation: Article II, Section 11 of the 1987 Constitution declares: 'The State values the dignity of every human person and guarantees full respect for human rights.' This provision mirrors the foundational human dignity principle of the UDHR and serves as a constitutional anchor for human rights protection in the Philippines.

subject: General Information
question: Under the 1987 Constitution, the Commission on Human Rights has the power to grant immunity from prosecution to witnesses. Under what condition may this power be exercised?

choices.text: When authorized by the President of the Philippines
When the witness is a foreign national
When the testimony or documents of the person are necessary or convenient to determine the truth in a CHR investigation
When the crime involved carries the death penalty

explanation: Article XIII, Section 18(8) of the 1987 Constitution provides that the CHR may 'Grant immunity from prosecution to any person whose testimony or whose possession of documents or other evidence is necessary or convenient to determine the truth in any investigation conducted by it or under its authority.' Presidential authorization is not required for this power.

subject: General Information
question: In the context of human rights, the principle of 'non-discrimination' holds that human rights belong to all persons without distinction. Which of the following best reflects this principle as applied in the Philippine setting?

choices.text: Only Filipino citizens enjoy the protection of the Bill of Rights
The CHR is mandated to provide legal protection to all persons within the Philippines, including Filipinos residing abroad
The State provides rights only to those who pay taxes
Human rights protection is limited to persons who are not disqualified by law

explanation: Article XIII, Section 18(3) mandates the CHR to 'Provide appropriate legal measures for the protection of human rights of all persons within the Philippines, as well as Filipinos residing abroad, and provide for preventive measures and legal aid services to the under-privileged.' This universal scope reflects the international principle of non-discrimination in human rights protection.

subject: General Information
question: Republic Act No. 9003, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, prohibits the establishment and operation of what type of waste disposal site after the law's effectivity?

choices.text: Sanitary landfills
Materials Recovery Facilities
Open dumps
Composting facilities

explanation: Section 37 of RA 9003 provides that 'No open dumps shall be established and operated, nor any practice or disposal of solid waste by any person, including LGUs, which constitutes the use of open dumps for solid wastes, be allowed after the effectivity of this Act.' Open dumps are prohibited because they cause serious environmental and health hazards.

subject: General Information
question: Under Republic Act No. 8749 (Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999), which of the following is generally banned by Section 20?

choices.text: The use of diesel engines in public vehicles
The use of coal as fuel in industrial plants
The import of second-hand motor vehicles
Incineration, defined as the burning of municipal, biomedical and hazardous waste which emits poisonous and toxic fumes

explanation: Section 20 of RA 8749 states that 'Incineration, hereby defined as the burning of municipal, biomedical and hazardous waste, which process emits poisonous and toxic fumes is hereby prohibited.' However, the prohibition does not apply to traditional small-scale community sanitation methods, traditional agricultural practices, crematoria, and similar exempted activities.

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 9003, LGUs that operate open dumps are required to convert these to controlled dumps within how many years after the law's effectivity, before controlled dumps are ultimately phased out?

choices.text: One year for conversion; controlled dumps phased out in two years
Three years for conversion; controlled dumps phased out in five years
Five years for conversion; controlled dumps phased out in seven years
Two years for conversion; controlled dumps phased out in four years

explanation: Section 37 of RA 9003 provides that 'within three (3) years after the effectivity of this Act, every LGU shall convert its open dumps into controlled dumps.' The same section further provides that 'no controlled dumps shall be allowed five (5) years following the effectivity of this Act,' setting a clear transition timeline toward sanitary landfills.

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 8749 (Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999), what document is the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) required to prepare annually to serve as the basis for the Integrated Air Quality Improvement Framework?

choices.text: The Annual Greenhouse Gas Inventory Report
The National Air Quality Status Report
The Environmental Compliance Certificate
The Annual Environmental Impact Assessment

explanation: Section 6 of RA 8749 requires the Department to 'prepare an annual National Air Quality Status Report which shall be used as the basis in formulating the Integrated Air Quality Improvement Framework.' This report must include relevant air quality data and will guide the formulation of air quality control action plans.

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 8749, what is an 'airshed' and on what basis shall its designation be made?

choices.text: A designated clean zone based on population density
A permitted emission corridor based on prevailing wind direction only
A geographic buffer zone surrounding industrial plants as required by DENR

An area designated on the basis of similar climate, meteorology, and topology which affect the interchange and diffusion of pollutants, or areas which share common interest or face similar development programs

explanation: Section 9 of RA 8749 defines airsheds and provides that their designation 'shall be on the basis of, but not limited to, areas with similar climate, meteorology and topology which affect the interchange and diffusion of pollutants in the atmosphere, or areas which share common interest or face similar development programs, prospects or problems.' This science-based approach allows for coordinated air quality management.

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 9003, a new solid waste management facility may not commence construction or operation until the proponent obtains what document from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources?

choices.text: A License to Operate (LTO) from the Department of Health
A Sanitary Permit from the local health office
An Environment Compliance Certificate (ECC) pursuant to Presidential Decree 1586
A Presidential Proclamation declaring the area suitable for waste disposal

explanation: Section 38 of RA 9003 provides that 'No person shall commence operation, including site preparation and construction of a new solid waste management facility or the expansion of an existing facility until said person obtains an Environment Compliance Certificate (ECC) from the Department pursuant to P.D. 1586 and other permits and clearances from concerned agencies.'

subject: General Information
question: The Philippine Clean Air Act (RA 8749) mandates local government units to promote what comprehensive program within their respective jurisdictions?

choices.text: Reforestation and watershed rehabilitation
Industrial emission reduction and permit compliance
Comprehensive ecological waste management including waste segregation, recycling, and composting
Establishment of air quality monitoring stations in every barangay

explanation: Section 20 of RA 8749 provides that 'Local government units are hereby mandated to promote, encourage and implement in their respective jurisdiction a comprehensive ecological waste management that includes waste segregation, recycling and composting.' This provision connects air quality goals with solid waste management at the local level.

subject: General Information
question: Under RA 8749, the Department of Energy (DOE), co-chaired by the DENR, is tasked to set specifications for all types of fuel and fuel-related products. These specifications shall be adopted by which body as Philippine National Standards?

choices.text: The Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (PNRI)
The Bureau of Product Standards (BPS) of the Department of Trade and Industry
The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC)
The Department of Science and Technology (DOST) alone

explanation: Section 26 of RA 8749 provides that the DOE, co-chaired by DENR, 'in consultation with the Bureau of Product Standards (BPS) of the DTI, the DOST, the representatives of the fuel and automotive industries, academe and the consumers shall set the specifications for all types of fuel and fuel-related products' and that 'the specifications...shall be adopted by the BPS as Philippine National Standards (PNS).'
